title.en: Explain a custom to a visitor
title.es: Explicar una costumbre a un visitante

es: Explicar una costumbre familiar a un visitante con generalizaciones matizadas, un ejemplo concreto y una comparación respetuosa.

teaching.en: Our Sunday lunch is an old custom and a long-standing tradition, and relatives tend to arrive around noon.
teaching.es: Nuestro almuerzo del domingo es una vieja costumbre y una tradición de larga data, y los parientes suelen llegar hacia el mediodía.
teaching.explanationEs: Se presenta la costumbre y se matiza con tend to.
segments: Our Sunday lunch is an old custom and a
long-standing tradition, and relatives tend to arrive around noon.
teaching.audioText: Our Sunday lunch is an old custom and a long-standing tradition, and relatives tend to arrive around noon.

teaching.en: By and large, a visitor is welcome at our table without an invitation, and a warm welcome is part of the custom.
teaching.es: En general, un visitante es bienvenido en nuestra mesa sin invitación, y una cálida bienvenida forma parte de la costumbre.
segments: By and large, a visitor is welcome at our table without
an invitation, and a warm welcome is part of the custom.
teaching.audioText: By and large, a visitor is welcome at our table without an invitation, and a warm welcome is part of the custom.

teaching.en: For example, we all share one big dish from the centre of the table as a gesture of hospitality.
teaching.es: Por ejemplo, todos compartimos un plato grande del centro de la mesa como gesto de hospitalidad.
teaching.explanationEs: For example introduce un ejemplo concreto que ilustra la costumbre.
segments: For example, we all share one big dish from the
centre of the table as a gesture of hospitality.
teaching.audioText: For example, we all share one big dish from the centre of the table as a gesture of hospitality.

teaching.en: Some cultures serve separate plates, whereas in mine the shared dish may strike a visitor as unusual at first.
teaching.es: Algunas culturas sirven platos separados, mientras que en la mía el plato compartido puede parecerle inusual a un visitante al principio.
teaching.explanationEs: Whereas contrasta dos costumbres sin juzgar ninguna.
segments: Some cultures serve separate plates, whereas in mine the shared
dish may strike a visitor as unusual at first.
teaching.audioText: Some cultures serve separate plates, whereas in mine the shared dish may strike a visitor as unusual at first.

teaching.en: A custom that is second nature to us is easy to overlook, but a visitor notices it at once.
teaching.es: Una costumbre que para nosotros es algo natural es fácil de pasar por alto, pero un visitante la nota de inmediato.
teaching.explanationEs: Lo automático para unos es lo llamativo para otros.
segments: A custom that is second nature to us is easy
to overlook, but a visitor notices it at once.
teaching.audioText: A custom that is second nature to us is easy to overlook, but a visitor notices it at once.

teaching.en: In many households it is customary to bring a small gift, and the host will share the best seat with a guest.
teaching.es: En muchas casas es costumbre llevar un pequeño regalo, y el anfitrión comparte el mejor asiento con el invitado.
teaching.explanationEs: It is customary to + verbo base: «es costumbre» sin culpar a nadie.
segments: In many households it is customary to bring a small gift,
and the host will share the best seat with a guest.
teaching.audioText: In many households it is customary to bring a small gift, and the host will share the best seat with a guest.

prompt.es: ¿Cómo debería corregir la estudiante esta explicación de su costumbre?

choices.text: In my country we eat at ten, which is obviously the only correct time for dinner.
In my country eating at six is strange, so you should really change your habit.
In my country nobody ever eats at six, unlike all other countries.
In my country families tend to eat at ten, whereas in yours it is earlier.

feedback.es: Tend to matiza la generalización y whereas contrasta sin juzgar; las demás versiones elogian la propia costumbre o rechazan la ajena.

hint.es: Busca la versión que describe la diferencia sin decir cuál es mejor.

origin.text: A student is describing the dinner time in her family: “In my country everybody eats dinner at ten, which is much better than the silly habit of eating at six.” Her teacher asks for a version that a visitor could hear without feeling hurt.

prompt.es: Completa: «El plato compartido puede parecerle inusual a un visitante.»

feedback.es: Strike someone as + adjetivo describe la impresión que algo causa a una persona, sin juzgar lo que es.

hint.es: Verbo que significa «golpear», pero aquí describe una impresión.

origin.text: In my house everybody shares one big dish, and this may ___ a visitor as unusual at first, although by the end of the evening it seems natural.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Ninguna forma es mejor porque cada costumbre tiene sentido en casa.»

answer.text: Neither way is better because each custom makes sense at home

feedback.es: Neither way is better + because + causa: la comparación respetuosa explica por qué no hay un ganador.

hint.es: Empieza con neither way y termina con at home.

prompt.es: Escucha: ¿qué actitud tiene quien narra hacia la costumbre de su abuela?

choices.text: It moves the narrator, although the cousins consider it odd.
It moves the narrator, and the cousins feel exactly the same.
It seems strange to the narrator, as it does to the cousins.
It worries the narrator whenever a visitor asks about it.

feedback.es: Contrasta con whereas: sus primos la consideran rara, pero a quien narra le emociona porque recuerda que la bienvenida no termina en la puerta.

origin.audio: My grandmother has a custom that surprises every visitor: before anyone eats, she puts a little food on a small plate by the window. She says it is a gesture of hospitality for anyone who might be passing. Whereas my cousins find it odd, I find it moving, because it reminds me that a welcome does not end at the front door.

prompt.es: Lee la situación: ¿qué frase compara dos costumbres con respeto?

choices.text: In my family we tend to sing first, which is obviously the correct way.
In my family we tend to sing first, whereas in many countries people cut the cake first.
In other countries people tend to cut the cake first, whereas we do it the right way.
Everybody in my family always sings first, unlike all other countries.

feedback.es: Tend to y whereas describen la diferencia sin juicio; las otras opciones, aunque usen las mismas estructuras, declaran una costumbre correcta o universal.

origin.text: A student is explaining to an exchange student how her family celebrates birthdays. She wants to describe the difference without sounding better than anybody else, and she is looking for the best sentence to use.

prompt.es: Ordena: «En general, los visitantes son bienvenidos a nuestra mesa.»

answer.text: By and large, visitors are welcome at our table

feedback.es: By and large abre la frase y matiza; visitors are welcome at our table es la generalización.

prompt.es: Escucha: ¿qué quiere transmitir quien habla al describir las costumbres de su casa?

choices.text: That visitors should copy her customs as soon as they arrive.
That her mother's kitchen rules are stricter than other families' rules.
That habits which look odd are gestures of welcome with their own logic.
That cooking together is a better custom than cooking alone.

feedback.es: Cada hábito que sorprende resulta ser un gesto de bienvenida con su lógica; la comparación final, «neither way is better», evita juzgar.

origin.audio: When visitors first come to my house, they usually notice three things: the shoes by the door, the very long goodbye and the fact that my mother will not let anyone help in the kitchen. At first glance these habits may strike them as strange. By and large, however, they leave understanding that each one is a gesture of welcome: the shoes keep the floor clean for the children, the long goodbye shows that nobody is in a hurry, and the empty kitchen is my mother's way of saying that a guest is a guest. Whereas in my friend's home everybody cooks together, in ours the cook is the host. Neither way is better; both are ways of saying: you matter.

prompt.es: ¿Qué corrección propone quien revisa el borrador?

choices.text: Delete the shared dish example because it is too personal.
Remove every comparison with other countries from the paragraph.
Soften “cold” to “a bit cold” so that the generalisation sounds fairer.
Replace the judgement by a description of behaviour.

feedback.es: Elogia el ejemplo y el tono cálido, pero el juicio «cold» sobre otras personas debe sustituirse por lo que hacen: describir conductas, no rasgos.

origin.text: Your paragraph about Sunday lunch is warm and vivid, and the example of the shared dish works well. However, the sentence “In other countries people are cold at meals” is an unfair generalisation, and it undermines the respectful tone of the rest. A better comparison would describe what people do, not what they are.

prompt.es: Completa: «En algunas casas es costumbre quitarse los zapatos al entrar.»

feedback.es: It is customary to + verbo base es la fórmula de registro más formal para «es costumbre».

origin.text: Guests do not always know the rules of a new house, but in some homes it is ___ to take off your shoes at the door, and a polite visitor does it without being asked.

prompt.es: Explica una costumbre de tu familia a un visitante (180–240 palabras).

answer.text: In my family, Friday dinner is a long-standing tradition. By and large, everybody is home by seven, and the children tend to choose the menu. For example, last week my little brother asked for rice and chicken, and we all agreed. A visitor is always welcome, and guests usually bring a dessert or a small gift. It is customary to share one big dish from the centre of the table, which may strike a visitor as unusual at first. In many countries each person has a separate plate, whereas in mine we pass the food around and talk while we eat. Neither way is better; each custom makes sense at home. Please do not worry if you are unsure what to do: my mother will show you, and she will give you a warm welcome. I hope that you can join us one Friday.
accepted: In my family, Friday dinner is a long-standing tradition. By and large, everybody is home by seven, and the children tend to choose the menu. For example, last week my little brother asked for rice and chicken, and we all agreed. A visitor is always welcome, and guests usually bring a dessert or a small gift. It is customary to share one big dish from the centre of the table, which may strike a visitor as unusual at first. In many countries each person has a separate plate, whereas in mine we pass the food around and talk while we eat. Neither way is better; each custom makes sense at home. Please do not worry if you are unsure what to do: my mother will show you, and she will give you a warm welcome. I hope that you can join us one Friday.

Every Sunday my family has lunch at my grandmother's house, a custom that is older than I am. As a rule, everybody arrives around noon, and the younger cousins tend to arrive last. For instance, last month my uncle brought a cake that he had baked himself, and we all laughed because it was still warm. Visitors are welcome too, and they usually sit next to my grandmother. In some countries people eat quickly and leave, whereas in mine the table is a place to stay and talk for hours. Neither way is wrong; each custom simply suits its own home. It may seem unusual at first, but guests quickly feel at ease. I would love to see you there one Sunday.

feedback.es: Un texto completo presenta la costumbre, matiza dos generalizaciones, da un ejemplo concreto y compara con respeto, sin juzgar.

origin.text: Explica a un visitante extranjero una costumbre de tu familia (la cena del viernes, el almuerzo del domingo…). Escribe en inglés con dos generalizaciones matizadas (by and large, tend to…), un ejemplo concreto y una comparación respetuosa con otra costumbre.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es la postura de quien escribe sobre explicar una costumbre a un extraño?

choices.text: Explaining a custom values it and welcomes strangers.
Explaining a custom makes it sound less natural, so it is best avoided.
Only customs that are very old deserve an explanation.
Strangers should learn the customs without asking questions.

feedback.es: Rebate la idea del museo: explicar con cariño mantiene viva la costumbre y abre la puerta al extraño.

origin.text: Some people claim that explaining a custom to a stranger makes it sound less natural, as if we were showing our family in a museum. I see it differently. A custom that we cannot explain is one that we have stopped noticing, and describing it kindly is a way of keeping it alive and of inviting the stranger in.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Mientras que nosotros compartimos un plato, ellos usan platos separados.»

answer.text: Whereas we share one dish, they use separate plates
accepted: Whereas we share one dish, they use separate plates
They use separate plates, whereas we share one dish

feedback.es: Whereas une dos hechos contrastados; puede abrir la frase o ir en medio, separado por coma.

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje: ¿qué actitud muestra Ana al explicar la costumbre?

choices.text: Formal: she lists conditions that Tom must accept to be welcome.
Relaxed and welcoming: she explains a habit, not a demand.
Nervous: she worries that Tom will dislike her family's customs.
Defensive: she justifies her family's habits before Tom can judge them.

feedback.es: Dice «not a rule, just a habit» y ofrece una solución si olvida algo: explica una costumbre con calidez y sin imponerla.

origin.audio: Hi Tom, it is Ana. About Saturday: at our house we tend to take off our shoes at the door, so bring some warm socks. It is not a rule, just a habit, and my mother will lend you some if you forget. She would be very happy if you tried her dessert, which is an old family recipe.
